o: Each operation changes x by ±1 and num by ∓1 simultaneously, so the gap |x − num| shrinks by exactly 2 per operation regardless of choices. To maximize x, always decrease x and increase num. After t operations starting from x = num + t (best initial guess), the gap closes completely: x_final = num + 2t. Example: num=3, t=2 → 3+4 = 7, matching the sample where x goes 5→7 while num goes 3→5→7... actually x=7, num becomes 7 after two ops.
k: Each operation reduces the difference |x − num| by exactly 2.
Optimal play: raise x by t before/while lowering it, yielding num + 2t.

a.i: Since each op closes the gap by 2 and we control direction, the maximum achievable x is simply num + 2·t.

w: Trivial once you see the gap shrinks by 2 per operation. Common confusion: misreading that num also changes — but since we choose directions, we can always push x up while pushing num up to meet it. No edge cases beyond the given constraints.
